language-tag finding: `"..."@lang` requires a LITERAL tag written in source -- the transpiler refuses a computed one (`@{key}` -> "'}' attendu pour fermer l'ilot de graphe", confirmed empirically on a standalone probe). Here `key` (the dict's language code, e.g. 'en'/'nb') is itself a runtime value, so the dedicated literal-suffix notation does not reach this site; the natural fallback is to keep building `Literal(self.subject[key], lang=key)` in plain Python and let `{expr}` in term position pass the already-built term through unchanged (node()'s documented pass-through for rdflib terms) -- not awkward, just a boundary of the @lang notation worth recording: a dict keyed by language code (SKOS/DCAT-style multilingual data) is exactly the shape where it doesn't apply
